title: Your Phone System Costs Way More Than You Think (And Nobody's Telling You)
excerpt: Hidden fees are eating your phone budget alive, and most small business owners have no idea how much they're actually paying.

content.text: So I've been looking at a bunch of VoIP pricing breakdowns this morning, and honestly? I'm getting frustrated on your behalf. Every platform — and I mean every single one — has this thing where the advertised price looks reasonable until you actually try to use it. Then suddenly there's per-user fees, per-feature fees, add-on costs, AI receptionist markups... it's like ordering a coffee and finding out the cup costs extra.

Here's what's happening: Most of these platforms publish a base price ($20-30 per user, usually), but that's basically a skeleton. The stuff you actually need — advanced call routing, analytics, decent voicemail features, customer service automation — that's where they get you. And because you're busy running your business, not pricing out phone systems, you don't realize you're paying double what you thought.
The Real Cost Looks Like This

items: Base per-user cost ($20-50/month depending on the platform)
Add-ons for AI features or advanced routing ($10-30 extra per user)
Setup fees (sometimes hidden in your first bill)
Integration costs if you want it connected to your CRM or other tools
International calling or SMS if you need those features
Customer support tiers if you actually want someone to pick up the phone when something breaks

content.text: A small business with 5 users thinking they're paying $25/person/month could easily end up at $50-60 per person once everything's added up. That's $1,500-1,800 a year in surprise costs.
Why This Actually Matters to You

You're probably comparing platforms based on that headline price, right? "Oh, this one's $29 and that one's $35, so obviously I should go with the cheaper one." But you're not comparing the same thing. It's like comparing car prices without knowing one includes the engine and the other one doesn't. By the time you get everything you actually need, you might be better off with the platform that looked more expensive at first.

content.label: Intecha's Take
content.text: Before you pick a phone system, ask the vendor for a full quote based on YOUR actual needs. Not their demo needs. Your needs. How many users? Do you need call recording? Do you want automated customer greetings? Do you need to integrate with your existing tools? Get them to put a total number in writing. If they're evasive about it, that's your sign to keep looking. You deserve to know what you're actually paying.

Also — and this is important — don't assume the fanciest platform is the right one. Sometimes a simpler system with transparent pricing is actually going to serve you better than the one with all the AI bells and whistles you don't need yet. You can always upgrade later. But you can't un-pay money you've already wasted on features gathering dust.
